t: LeetCode 2247 - Maximum Cost of Trip With K Highways: Bitmask Dynamic Programming
o: **Understanding the problem.** We need a maximum-toll simple walk with exactly k edges over at most 15 cities - the classic setting for bitmask DP. The state is (set of visited cities, current city) and transitions append an unvisited neighbor. A trip crossing k highways visits k + 1 distinct cities, so any k >= n is immediately impossible. Example 1 finds 0 -> 1 -> 4 -> 3 totaling 17; example 2 has two disconnected components that are too small, giving -1. With 2^15 masks, 15 endpoints, and 15 extensions each, the DP performs roughly seven million operations, whereas naive DFS over permutations explodes combinatorially on dense graphs.
k: n <= 15 signals bitmask DP: encode the visited set in 15 bits.
Exactly-k-edge trips need k+1 distinct cities, so k >= n implies -1 outright.
Final candidates are DP states whose mask holds exactly k+1 cities.

a.n: Approach 1: DFS over All Simple Walks (Brute Force)
a.i: Launch a backtracking walk from every city, marking visited cities in a bitmask and stopping once exactly k edges are traversed. It is exponential in the worst case - a dense graph with k = 14 approaches factorial path counts - but it is short to write and validates correctness of the DP.
s: From every start city, recurse: if no edges remain, record the accumulated cost.
Otherwise extend to every unvisited neighbor with cost plus its toll.
Return the best recorded cost, or -1 if no full-length walk exists.
a.t: Exponential - up to O(n!) walks on dense graphs, impractical beyond tiny inputs.
a.sp: O(n + E) - recursion depth plus adjacency lists.

a.n: Approach 2: Bitmask DP over (Visited Set, Last City)
a.i: Define dp[mask][i] as the best cost of a simple walk visiting exactly the cities in mask and currently standing at i. Singletons seed zero, and relaxing dp[mask | 1<<j][j] over unvisited neighbors builds all walks in increasing-mask order. Finally read off states whose mask contains exactly k + 1 cities.
s: If `k >= n`, return -1; build an adjacency/toll matrix.
Iterate masks ascending; from each reachable `(mask, i)`, extend to every city `j` outside the mask with an edge to `i`.
Answer with the maximum `dp[mask][i]` over masks of popcount `k + 1`, or -1 if none exists.
a.t: O(2^n * n^2) - every mask-endpoint pair scans n candidate extensions; about 7 x 10^6 steps at n = 15.
a.sp: O(2^n * n) - the DP table itself.

w: State the early exit for k >= n and the popcount-(k+1) readout precisely - those are where implementations slip. Watch sentinel initialization in languages without an infinity value: use INT_MIN / 2 so adding nonnegative tolls cannot overflow. Follow-ups: the minimum-cost twin uses the identical skeleton, asking for exactly k cities shifts popcount bookkeeping by one, and reconstructing the itinerary requires storing predecessors per state.
